newsitem.title: USA: Judge to set date for Jones-Clinton trial.
newsitem.headline: Judge to set date for Jones-Clinton trial.

text.p: A U.S. federal judge said on Thursday she would set a trial date in Paula Jones' sexual harassment case against President Bill Clinton during a hearing scheduled for Aug. 22 in Little Rock.
The date for the hearing was announced in an order by U.S. District Judge Susan Webber Wright.
A status conference to schedule legal proceedings and set a trial date in the case had been requested by attorneys on both sides, according to the order.
Jones has accused Clinton of pressuring her to perform a sex act with him at a Little Rock hotel in May 1991 while he was governor of Arkansas and she was a state employee.
Clinton has denied the allegations and his attorneys have tried to postpone the lawsuit until he leaves the White House.
Clinton's lawyers earlier this month asked the judge to postpone the discovery process in the case until she had ruled on their motion that the lawsuit be dismissed.
